items.title: 6. Pricing engine (as-built)
items.text: Deterministic, rules-based, no runtime AI. Implementation: backend/app/services/price_calc.py. Spec: Annex One §6/§10 for the formula and confidence factors; the Canonical Pricing Specification (CPS) for pricing item definitions, trigger conditions, consumer question copy and Price Item display names. Breakdown lines are labelled with the CPS Price Item names via the single CPS_DISPLAY_NAMES map (raw Master Export column string → display name).

items.title: Constants (as-built)
items.text: Constant Code value Notes CONFIDENCE_UPLIFT_C 0.20 Estimated legal-fee uplift (Annex One §10); set by engine-tweaks.md. CONFIDENCE_UPLIFT_D 0.02 Per-item estimated-disbursement uplift (§6) VAT_RATE 0.20 On legal fees only (not on HMLR / VAT-free searches) ANCHORS 150k, 250k, 500k, 750k, 1m, 1.25m, 1.5m Seven CML anchor points

items.title: Formula
items.text:
P_estimated       = anchor_fee + Σ applicable modifiers + Σ applicable additional costs
P_legal_effective = P_estimated × (1 + 0.20)   if price_type = estimated
                  = P_estimated                if price_type = verified
P_effective       = P_legal_effective + (P_legal_effective × 0.20 VAT) + Σ included disbursements
  • Anchor lookup (_nearest_anchor): the user's property value snaps to the closest of the seven anchors by absolute distance (nearest, not round-up).
  • Modifiers applied (purchase): new-build (freehold), new-lease (leasehold), acting-for-lender (when mortgage), shared ownership / HTB equity loan / HTB ISA (three independent CPS split flags), gifted deposit, unregistered-title purchase, Building Safety Act / Higher-Risk Building (leasehold AND answer Yes), Solar Panels (answer Yes), Freehold Management Company (freehold AND answer Yes), Existing Tenancy (checkbox true). (Sale): unregistered-title sale, additional mortgage redemption (modifier × (n − 1) for mortgage_redemption_count n > 1 — the first redemption is in the base fee), BSA (leasehold AND Yes), Solar Panels (answer Yes), Help to Buy Redemption (checkbox true). Unregistered-title fires on a No answer to the registered-title question; a Don't know answer never applies a modifier. Zero-amount lines are dropped from display. "Leasehold supplement" is imported onto every card but deliberately never applied by any trigger — the LHP/LHS anchor grids already carry the leasehold premium for most firms, so applying it again would double-count; revisit pending founder confirmation.
  • Additional costs applied: Identity Verification (firm amount × party count, "Four or more" = ×4, charged once per transaction — purchase side on combined), onboarding, transfer-admin (both sides), file storage (wherever the firm records one; never user-gated); SDLT admin (purchase).
  • Disbursements (purchase side only): the CML standard search pack — honouring its per-item estimated (+2% d) and vat_applies flags — plus the HM Land Registry Scale 1 (online) registration fee (a known, VAT-free, non-estimated public fee: ≤£80k→£20, ≤£100k→£40, ≤£200k→£100, ≤£500k→£150, ≤£1m→£295, >£1m→£500). The CPS HMLR sale-side fee is not implemented (calculation undefined in the CPS).
  • Breakdown grouping: quote lines are returned in three lists matching the CPS categories — adjustments (legal-fee modifiers), additional_costs, disbursements.
  • Combined buy+sell: the pricer runs once per side and sums the two totals (both sides carry their own VAT; disbursements arise on the purchase side only).
  • A firm with no anchors for the tenure/side, an unpriceable intake, or price_type = no_data returns no quote and is dropped from results.

Pending CPS updates: the "Don't know" pricing consequence beyond "never apply the modifier" still awaits a CPS update (issue #55; the Solar Panels, Freehold Management Company, Existing Tenancy and Help to Buy Redemption modifiers are priced as of the 07.07.26 Master Export).

Worked end-to-end examples: docs/ranking-algorithm-worked-examples.md.

items.title: 7. Ranking engine (as-built)
items.text: Deterministic six-factor scorecard. Identical inputs always produce identical outputs. Implementation: ranking.py (factor scorers), scorecard.py (weights + tie-break), search.py (orchestration). Spec: Annex One §5–§16.

items.title: Factor scoring
items.text:
Factor Input Basis Reputation organisations.adjusted_reputation_value Relative min–max across the result set (all-equal ⇒ 50) Price Total Effective Price (§6) Relative inverse min–max — lower price scores higher (all-equal ⇒ 50) Complaints complaints_summary.score Absolute, consumed directly (missing ⇒ 100) Regulatory regulatory_summary.score Absolute, consumed directly (missing ⇒ 100) Distance nearest office (haversine, miles) Banded: 0–2→100, 2–5→95, 5–10→85, 10–15→70, 15–25→50, 25–40→25, 40+→10 Offices office count Banded: 1→70, 2–3→78, 4–6→85, 7–10→90, 11–20→95, 21+→100

Distance is banded by miles, not min–max normalised (changed per engine-tweaks.md). Bands are lower-bound-inclusive top-down (exactly 2.0mi → 95).

items.title: Scorecards (scorecard.py::SCORECARDS, integer weights summing to 100)
items.text:
Variant Rep Price Compl Reg Dist Off balanced 27 23 15 15 10 10 reputation 40 20 12 12 8 8 price 20 40 12 12 8 8 complaints 18 18 40 10 7 7 regulatory 18 18 10 40 7 7 distance 17 17 10 10 40 6 offices 17 17 10 10 6 40

The user picks one priority factor on the chat preference step (default balanced).

  • Distance excluded (no postcode, or include_distance=false, or a postcode that fails to geocode): distance weight → 0 and the remaining weights are proportionately rescaled to sum to 100 (Annex One §8.2). When a postcode fails to geocode, the consumer is told why via distance_status (postcode_not_found / geocoding_unavailable) and offered an inline re-entry / retry on the results page (issue #182, D-1).
  • Overall score = Σ(factor × weight) / 100.
  • Tie-break order (§11): overall → reputation → complaints → regulatory → price → distance score → offices → alphabetical by firm name.

items.title: Sequencing & eligibility (search.py)
items.text:
1. Eligibility filter (upstream of scoring): exclude organisations.excluded = true. Firms without a usable price card (no card, price_type = no_data, or an intake that cannot be priced) are included but ranked after all priceable firms with quote = null and factor_scores.price = null (§8.13). They are not eligible for the top-5 contactable set.
  2. Rank the entire in-scope WMCA market with the chosen scorecard.
  3. Extract the top 5 contactable from that ordering: enrolled = true AND active_in_pilot = true, first five in rank order. Firms ranked 6+ (or not contactable) are shown without Proceed/ Callback actions. This preserves the "whole of market / independent" positioning.

No per-CTA gating. Proceed/Callback availability is driven solely by enrolled + active_in_pilot + top-5 membership (results) and an enrolled check (submit endpoints). There is no per-firm "Proceed enabled" / "Callback enabled" switch — the earlier vestigial proceed_enabled / callback_enabled columns were removed. Per-CTA control would need wiring into search.py and the appointment endpoints.

Distance deep-dive: docs/architecture/postcode-distance.md.

items.title: 8. Google lead generation (Google Ads click-ID attribution)
items.text: PPC (Google Ads) is the pilot's traffic source. CML captures the ad click ID on landing, ties it to the lead it produces, and can hand that back to the agency for an offline "Import conversions from clicks" upload. There is no server-side conversion postback, no gtag/GA4, and no UTM parsing — attribution is purely on the Google click ID, exported and uploaded out-of-band.

items.title: What is captured
items.text:
Parameter When Google uses it gclid Standard Google Ads click ID (the common case) gbraid iOS traffic, app→web journeys wbraid iOS traffic, web→web journeys

Whichever is present in the landing URL is read verbatim (e.g. https://choosemylawyer.ai/?gclid=…). Capture is site-wide — the ad's final URL can point at any page. UTM params are not captured.

items.title: Where it is stored (three stages — frontend/lib/clickIds.ts → DB)
items.text:
1. Browser, on landing — <ClickIdCapture /> (mounted in the root layout) writes any present click ID to a first-party cookie (sozo_gclid / sozo_gbraid / sozo_wbraid, 90-day max-age) with a localStorage mirror. Capture is unconditional — NOT gated by cookie consent (so attribution survives a declined banner), and only writes when a param is present (inert for organic/direct). The Meta Pixel / analytics tracking in §9 is consent-gated; this is the deliberate exception.
  2. Chat session, on intake start — stamped onto chat_sessions.{gclid,gbraid,wbraid}; the session created_at is the landing-stage capture time.
  3. Lead, on conversion — at Proceed/Callback the current click ID is read again and stamped onto appointments.{gclid,gbraid,wbraid} plus click_captured_at (conversion time), alongside the firm and quoted_price (conversion value). Storing at both stages lets attribution survive if one stage missed it.

A Proceed is one lead (appointments.type = select); a Callback to up to three firms produces one lead row per firm, all sharing the same click ID and click_captured_at.

items.title: Lead export for the agency
items.text:
The click-ID data is captured on every session and lead, but there is no self-serve "download leads CSV" yet — for the pilot the export is produced on request from the production DB with the query below.

Attribution rules (decided 2026-07, issue #53):

  1. One conversion per user submission, not per firm. A callback to up to three firms is a single user action on one ad click, so it uploads as one CML Callback conversion (the DB still holds one appointments row per firm — the grouping happens at export). A Proceed is one conversion as before. Per-firm rows would triple-count callback clicks in Google Ads.
  2. conversion_value = highest quoted_price in the submission (MAX). The consumer transacts with at most one firm, so the value a click can realise is a single quote, not the sum of the bundle; summing would inflate callbacks ~3× relative to Proceeds and bias bidding towards the less-committed action. For Proceeds (single row) this degenerates to the row's own quote, keeping the two conversion actions directly comparable.
  3. conversion_time is emitted as yyyy-mm-dd HH:mm:ss+HH:mm in UTC (offset +00:00), one of Google's accepted click-import formats — no timezone ambiguity at upload.

The rules are interdependent: per-submission grouping (1) forces an aggregate value rule (2) and a single timestamp per row (3). Do not change one without revisiting the others.

SELECT
    a.session_id                      AS session_id,
    a.type                            AS lead_type,         -- 'select' (Proceed) or 'callback'
    CASE a.type WHEN 'select' THEN 'CML Proceed'
                WHEN 'callback' THEN 'CML Callback' END     AS conversion_name,
    COALESCE(a.gclid,  s.gclid)       AS gclid,             -- conversion-time value, else landing value
    COALESCE(a.gbraid, s.gbraid)      AS gbraid,
    COALESCE(a.wbraid, s.wbraid)      AS wbraid,
    to_char(MIN(COALESCE(a.click_captured_at, a.created_at)) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC',
            'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS') || '+00:00'            AS conversion_time,
    MAX(a.quoted_price)               AS conversion_value,  -- GBP; highest quote in the submission
    'GBP'                             AS conversion_currency,
    COUNT(*)                          AS firms_contacted,   -- 1 for Proceed, 1–3 for Callback
    string_agg(o.cml_firm_id, '; ' ORDER BY o.cml_firm_id)  AS firm_ids,
    string_agg(a.id::text,    '; ' ORDER BY o.cml_firm_id)  AS lead_ids,
    s.created_at                      AS session_started_at -- landing-stage capture time
FROM appointments a
LEFT JOIN chat_sessions s ON s.id = a.session_id
JOIN organisations  o ON o.id = a.org_id
WHERE a.created_at >= :from_date AND a.created_at < :to_date   -- half-open range
GROUP BY a.session_id, a.type, a.click_captured_at,
         COALESCE(a.gclid,  s.gclid),
         COALESCE(a.gbraid, s.gbraid),
         COALESCE(a.wbraid, s.wbraid),
         s.created_at
ORDER BY conversion_time;
-- Google-attributable rows only: add
--   AND COALESCE(a.gclid,a.gbraid,a.wbraid,s.gclid,s.gbraid,s.wbraid) IS NOT NULL

Grouping grain caveats: a.click_captured_at is in the key because it is stamped once per submission (shared by every row of a callback bundle, distinct for a later Proceed in the same session). Since issue #176, only one Select can be live on a session (or consumer email) at a time — a second Proceed attempted while the first is still live is refused before an appointment is even created, so it never reaches this export. A second Proceed genuinely submitted later, once the first referral has been released (unable_to_act, not_instructed, completed, aborted or an admin void), is a distinct submission with its own click_captured_at, so the grouping grain still keeps the two apart rather than merging them. Rows whose session_id was nulled by a session deletion (ON DELETE SET NULL) group only by click ID and submission time; with no click ID at all they are excluded by the attributable-rows filter above, which is the only variant uploaded to Google.

The columns Google requires for the click-import are the click ID, conversion_name, conversion_time, conversion_value, conversion_currency; the rest (session_id, lead_type, firms_contacted, firm_ids, lead_ids, session_started_at) are for CML/agency reconciliation only.

items.title: Importing into Google Ads (agency)
items.text: Standard offline conversion import keyed on click ID (Goals → Conversions → New → Import → "Conversions from clicks"): - Create one conversion action per CML action — CML Proceed, CML Callback. - Multi-firm callbacks are already de-duplicated by the export (one row per submission — see the attribution rules in §8.3). As belt-and-braces, still set CML Callback to count "One" per click in the conversion-action settings. - Conversion time is emitted by the export as yyyy-mm-dd HH:mm:ss+00:00 (UTC offset included), which Google accepts directly — no account-timezone reconciliation needed. - Click-ID match window is ~90 days (Google-side); CML's 90-day cookie retention is aligned, but very delayed conversions may fall outside Google's window.

items.title: Privacy position
items.text:
The click-ID cookie is first-party and holds only the opaque Google identifier — no name/email/phone. Personal details are captured separately at conversion under explicit data-sharing consent and are not part of the Google Ads feed (click ID + conversion metadata only). Meta Pixel / funnel analytics (§9) are consent-gated and independent of this attribution.

Google ad click ─ ?gclid=… ─► Landing: click ID → first-party cookie (90d, no consent gate)
        └─► Intake started → stamped on chat_session
              └─► Proceed / Callback → stamped on lead (+ click_captured_at, firm, quoted_price)
                    └─► Export (click ID · conversion name · time · GBP value) → Google Ads click import

items.title: Legacy — Google Places reviews sync (retired)
items.text: Reputation now arrives pre-baked in the Master Export (adjusted_reputation_value), so the weekly Google Places sync was removed (see app/tasks/scheduler.py). GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY and the reviews.external_id / reviews.synced_at columns (the sync's idempotency/audit fields) have now been removed too. The review_source enum keeps its google value — pre-baked Google ratings still display on results and in the firm portal.

items.title: 9. Analytics & tracking
items.text:
Consent split (issue #120, D-7). The first-party mirror is essential and fires regardless of consent (anonymous, first-party, never leaves CML); the marketing streams (Meta Pixel, GTM/dataLayer) remain gated on marketing consent (frontend/lib/consent.ts, localStorage key cml.cookieConsent). frontend/lib/analytics.ts::emit always calls mirrorToBackend, then returns early before the Pixel/dataLayer pushes when consent is absent. The cookie notice wording reflects this (essential anonymous analytics vs consented marketing).

  • Meta Pixel (components/MetaPixel.tsx) — loads only when NEXT_PUBLIC_META_PIXEL_ID is set and consent is accepted. Standard events: PageView, Lead (Proceed), Contact (Callback). Custom events: IntakeStarted, IntakeCompleted, ScorecardChosen, ResultsViewed. First-party-only events (intake_step, evidence_link_clicked) have no Meta mapping.
  • Google Tag Manager (components/GoogleTagManager.tsx) — container injected only when NEXT_PUBLIC_GTM_ID is set and consent is accepted (re-checked live on consent change). Tag configuration lives in the GTM console, not in code.
  • First-party mirror (frontend/lib/analytics.ts → POST /api/public/events → analytics_events) — events captured server-side so the founder has Meta-independent data. Event types: page_view, intake_started, intake_step, intake_completed, scorecard_chosen, results_viewed, evidence_link_clicked, select_clicked, select_gateway_accepted, select_gateway_declined, select, callback, interest_registered. (proceed is accepted by the backend schema as a legacy alias but is no longer emitted by the frontend — select is the current Proceed event type.) Every event carries an anonymous visitor_id (frontend/lib/visitor.ts, localStorage cml.visitorId) for distinct-user counting. intake_step carries {question_id, step} (intake drop-off); evidence_link_clicked carries {org_id, source} (SRA/LeO/reviews outbound-link usage on the results page).
  • Select Confirmation Gateway funnel (issue #189), all carrying {org_id, quoted_price}: select_clicked — the Select button was pressed and the gateway opened; select_gateway_accepted — the consumer confirmed and continued to the Select form; select_gateway_declined — the consumer explicitly backed out (secondary control, Escape or backdrop), which is what distinguishes declining from abandoning at the gateway. select_clicked → select_gateway_accepted → select (Select form completed) is the drop-off funnel; grouping the declines on metadata.org_id in the CSV export gives declines per firm.

Traffic source. UTM params + external referrer are captured on landing (frontend/lib/trafficSource.ts, sessionStorage), attached to the chat session at creation, and stored on chat_sessions (utm_source/medium/campaign, referrer) alongside the Google Ads click IDs (§8).

Export: GET /api/admin/analytics/export?from=&to= (admin-keyed) returns a CSV of events for the half-open [from, to) date range.

items.title: Operations dashboard & data metrics (issues #74, #120)
items.text:
app/api/admin/metrics.py + components/admin/AdminDashboard.tsx. All read-only aggregates over the tables above; every endpoint takes the same half-open [from, to) window.

  • GET /metrics/summary — funnel (incl. unique_users, per-question intake_steps), a commercial block (participating / chargeable / deferred firm counts, estimated referral revenue), lead-quality, marketing (traffic_sources, evidence_sources, matter types, top pages) and Google-Ads attribution.
  • GET /metrics/firms — Participating-firm leaderboard (enrolled only): selects, callback leads, pipeline value, searches_appeared, and firm response times (referral → conflict-check / contact report, from workflow_events). Filters: from, to, org_id.
  • GET /metrics/non-participating — un-enrolled firms with searches appeared, interest registrations and latest consumer search; default order searches-appeared desc, tie-break latest-search desc (D-8). Filters: from, to, org_id.
  • GET /metrics/ledger — chargeable-events (appointment) ledger.
  • CSV exports (underlying rows, respecting active filters): /metrics/firms/export, /metrics/non-participating/export, /metrics/rankings/export (search ranking-position events), /metrics/ledger/export, plus /analytics/export.

Commercial model. Referral revenue = 15% of net legal fees (appointments.legal_fee_net = base fee + modifiers + additional costs, excluding the estimated-confidence uplift, VAT and all disbursements — captured at conversion) summed over matters in instruction_accepted / pre_exchange / contracts_exchanged (D-1/D-2). Subscription revenue = chargeable firms × £200/month (D-3). A firm becomes Chargeable the first time any of its transactions reaches instruction_accepted (organisations.chargeable_since, set once by app/services/workflow.py). The commercial block is a current-state snapshot and is not date-filtered.

Durable ranking positions. Every completed default (balanced) search records one search_ranking_events row per in-scope firm — including non-participating firms — grouped by a search_id (app/api/public/search.py). This is the underlying event data behind "searches appeared" and "latest consumer search"; it is exported, never presented raw.

items.title: 10. DNS & email configuration
items.text:
Transactional email is sent via SparkPost from a dedicated send-only subdomain mail.choosemylawyer.ai, kept entirely separate from the Microsoft 365 mailboxes on the root @choosemylawyer.ai. Full record-level runbook: docs/dns-email-configuration.md.

Concern Value Provider / sending domain SparkPost · mail.choosemylawyer.ai From address / name noreply@mail.choosemylawyer.ai · Choose My Lawyer Audit BCC CML_AUDIT_EMAIL (must be a deliverable M365 mailbox, e.g. leads@choosemylawyer.ai) DKIM scph0626._domainkey.mail TXT Return-path / SPF alignment CNAME mail → sparkpostmail.com (strict alignment) DMARC root _dmarc p=quarantine (enforcing; relaxed alignment covers the subdomain)

Settings (config.py): SPARKPOST_API_KEY (empty ⇒ mock mode, logs only), SPARKPOST_FROM_EMAIL (default noreply@mail.choosemylawyer.ai), SPARKPOST_FROM_NAME (default Choose My Lawyer), CML_AUDIT_EMAIL (empty ⇒ no BCC).

"In the user's name" mechanic (email.py): firm-facing Proceed/Callback emails set from_name = the consumer's name, reply_to = the consumer's email, and bcc = the audit mailbox — so the firm sees the consumer in their inbox and Reply goes straight to them, while CML keeps an audit copy. Firm mail reaches a firm only via organisation.referral_email.

⚠️ Because DMARC is enforcing, mail must send from @mail.choosemylawyer.ai. Until DKIM verifies (dkim_status: valid), SparkPost signs with its shared domain → DMARC fails → spam. Verify DKIM via the API, not the dashboard button (see the runbook).

items.title: 11. Email workflow & scheduler (issues #94/#96/#97/#155)
items.text:
Canonical copy/trigger/suppression spec: docs/email-spec.md (verbatim, with the [D-n] triage decisions applied). End-to-end lifecycle diagram: docs/email-workflow-diagram.md. This section is the as-built summary. The retired Phase F follow-up jobs (followups.py / followup_tokens.py) are fully superseded by this system.

Issue #155: a SparkPost 500 on a Firm-01 referral was logged and dropped with no retry, no recorded reason and no alert. send_email (app/services/email.py) now classifies, retries and alerts on every send in this section — see "Send retry, failure classification and alerting" below.

items.title: Workflow states (appointments.workflow_state)
items.text:
Every Select instruction and every per-firm Callback request is one appointments row — its id is the CML Transaction ID — holding exactly one state, advanced only by app/services/workflow.py (which also appends one immutable workflow_events audit row per action: channel, actor, timestamp, detail, free-text note, and — where the action changes an already-recorded status — the mandatory reason for the change, issue #57).

State Meaning referred Initial state — referral sent, no outcome reported instruction_accepted Firm reported the instruction effective — matter open, Firm-05 cycle starts unable_to_act Conflict or other valid reason (Non-Instruction Declaration recorded) unable_to_contact Two contact attempts failed (callback only) not_instructed Contact made, not instructed / engagement docs issued but not proceeding pre_exchange → contracts_exchanged Matter stages — forward-only; re-confirming the current stage is a valid periodic report completed / aborted Terminal — set by the Final Matter Report, which also stamps appointments.billing_eligible_at voided Terminal — a CML admin action (issue #176), never a firm-reported outcome; releases the one-live-Select block, sends no email, and is excluded from the billing export

Reopen: a not_instructed referral can be reopened (subsequent instruction) to instruction_accepted — same transaction id, attribution and history, never a new referral; the Firm-05 schedule restarts from the reopen date.

One live Select per consumer (issue #176): referred, instruction_accepted, pre_exchange and contracts_exchanged are the live states (LIVE_STATES in app/services/workflow.py) — while a consumer's Select is in one of them, POST /api/public/appointments refuses a further Select for that session or that email address (case/whitespace-insensitive), even for the same firm, with a 409. Every other state releases the block, including voided. An admin can void a live Select from the Operations Dashboard (POST /api/admin/appointments/{id}/void, reason required) — silent (no consumer/firm email) and excluded from the chargeable-events CSV export.

items.title: Engagement Log (/engagement-log, issue #161)
items.text:
A read-only firm-portal page (top-level, not nested under /analytics) listing every Callback and Select for the signed-in firm, newest first, paginated — reusing GET /api/firm/analytics/engagements unchanged. Two columns beyond the existing set: the CML Transaction ID (the appointment id, copyable) and a plain-English workflow_state label covering all ten states (derive_firm_status_label in app/services/workflow.py — distinct from the consumer-facing, lossy status_label in workflow_emails.py). conflict_check_outcome also now falls back to unable_to_act ⇒ "conflict" when no admin conflict check is recorded (derive_conflict_check_outcome), consistent across four surfaces that must stay in lockstep: the firm portal, the admin ledger (JSON + CSV) and the admin summary "Conflict checks" tile — the last of which re-derives the same rule in SQL in app/api/admin/metrics.py rather than calling the helper.

Outcome reporting from the portal (issue #57). The Engagement Log is now also a write surface — the second firm reporting route alongside the tokenised email links (D-1), not a replacement for them. Three endpoints, all authenticated with get_current_user and 404-ing (never 403) on another firm's referral: GET /api/firm/engagements/{id}/reporting (status, outcome options + flow requirements, current status label, and the full workflow_events audit trail oldest-first, with note returned only on firm-authored (email/portal) events so consumer comments and CML void reasons never reach the firm), POST /api/firm/engagements/{id}/outcome and POST /api/firm/engagements/{id}/conflict-check (which notifies the consumer on conflict through the same email.schedule_conflict_check_failed helper as the admin route). The rules — option set, Non-Instruction Declaration, judgment gate, two-attempts confirmation, acknowledgement copy, error codes — live once in app/services/firm_reporting.py and are shared with app/api/public/workflow_responses.py, so the two routes cannot drift; both dispatch the same dispatch_outcome_emails background task after commit, and both write the same appointments.workflow_state, so the daily email cycle's referred gate suppresses Firm-02/04, their reminders and exceptions whichever route reported.

Portal writes are audited with channel = portal and the signed-in firm user's email as the actor (D-8). Latest report wins (D-3): a report that changes an already-recorded status takes effect from either route, but requires a brief free-text reason (D-4) — kept in the new workflow_events.reason column alongside the previous status, the new status, the timestamp, the route and the user. Nothing is overwritten: every report appends one row under the same outcome_recorded action key. Re-reporting the outcome already recorded is a 409 already_recorded, a change with no reason a 422 reason_required, and completed / aborted / voided (TERMINAL_STATES) a 409 closed directing the firm to CML (D-7).

items.title: Email inventory (template keys as written to email_events)
items.text:
Sender identity (D-7): everything is sent from CML; the two referral emails carry reply-to = consumer. The canonical Transaction Summary is rendered in full at the bottom of every email (D-8).

Template Trigger Suppressed when consumer_01 / firm_01 Callback request created (immediate) — consumer_07 / firm_03 Select instruction created (immediate) — firm_02 / firm_04 3rd / 10th working day after referral outcome already recorded consumer_02 4th working day after callback submission (D-5; one per submission) every outcome recorded, or any firm instructed consumer_08 5th working day after select instruction outcome recorded consumer_03 / consumer_04 / consumer_06 Firm records unable-to-act / unable-to-contact / not-instructed another firm on the submission already instructed (consumer_06/others) consumer_05 Firm records instruction accepted (either workflow); carries the CML feedback link second instruction on the same submission consumer_09 Select firm unable to act; carries Contact CML (D-10) + tokenised results return (D-11) — firm_05_p{n} Matter progress request: 10 weeks after instruction accepted, then monthly anniversaries of the instruction date, per period n, while the matter is open stage update already recorded in that reporting period (either channel); ceases at completed/aborted consumer_10 / consumer_11 Firm records matter completed / aborted via the Final Matter Report (issue #131) a review is already captured for the transaction *_reminder One per reporting action: Consumer-02 +5d, Consumer-05 +14d, Consumer-08 +5d, Consumer-10 +14d, Consumer-11 +21d (calendar); Firm-02/04 +5wd, Firm-05 +10wd action completed or state moved on firm_exception / firm_05_p{n}_exception Firm reminder unanswered after 5 further working days → one email to CML_EXCEPTION_EMAIL; automation for that action ends action completed after the reminder contact_cml Consumer submits the tokenised Contact CML form —

Consumer-10/11 (matter completed/aborted review emails, issue #131 — [D-3 lifted: capture-only]) are live: the Final Matter Report submission (above) sends the appropriate email, whose link opens a login-free, tokenised /review/{token} journey capturing one structured review per transaction — three star ratings plus price-integrity answers, free text kept separate — into the consumer_reviews table (§5). Capture-only means exactly that: the review is stored against the transaction and surfaced nowhere else — it is never published, never joins reviews, and feeds neither the ranking nor the displayed reputation aggregate, nor a firm notification. Firm-06 (review notification) and review publication (public display, moderation, firm responses) remain deferred (D-3).

Standalone sends (issue #155): four CML sends outside the workflow above previously wrote no email_events row at all — conflict_check_failed, enrollment_invitation, user_invitation, password_reset (app/services/email.py), each written with appointment_id NULL. Kept outside the consumer_*/firm_* prefixes above so the admin log's prefix-match template filter is unaffected.

items.title: Action tokens
items.text:
Every actionable email link carries a stateless HMAC-signed token (app/services/action_tokens.py): action + appointment id + expiry (+ optional context), signed with SECRET_KEY. TTL 60 days for firm reporting (firm_report, matter_report), feedback, Contact CML and the review link (review, issue #131 — long enough for the Consumer-11 reminder at 21 days plus a usable window after it); 30 days for consumer response and results-return links. Replay of a completed action is rejected by the state machine (friendly 409), not the token. Backend response surfaces (app/api/public/workflow_responses.py, mounted at /api/public/workflow/): /firm-report/{token}, /matter-report/{token}, /progress/{token}, /contact-check/{token}, /feedback/{token}, /contact-cml/{token}, /results-return/{token}, /review/{token} (GET context + POST submit) — the frontend page paths for the latter two are named /update-progress/{token} and /return/{token} (§4).

The matter-report flow records pre-exchange / contracts-exchanged in one click; completed/aborted continue seamlessly into the Final Matter Report on the same page (outcome pre-populated and amendable, matter dates, final legal fee or confirmed none, price comparison vs the CML estimate with a reason when changed). Submission closes the workflow state, writes the full report detail to the audit trail and stamps billing_eligible_at.

items.title: Scheduler cycle
items.text: One idempotent pass (app/services/email_cycle.py::run_email_cycle), run daily at 09:00 Europe/London by the in-process APScheduler (app/tasks/scheduler.py). Whether an email is due is derived only from the current workflow state and working-day arithmetic (England & Wales bank holidays hardcoded in callback_windows.py); the email-event log is consulted to dedupe — via workflow_emails.already_attempted, true only once a sent row exists, so a genuinely successful (transaction, template) pair is attempted at most once — and, for a failed row, via workflow_emails.should_attempt (issue #155), which governs retry eligibility instead (below). The log also anchors reminder/exception timing to the actual send date.

items.title: Send retry, failure classification and alerting (issue #155)
items.text:
send_email (app/services/email.py) covers every send in this section, including the standalone sends above — one implementation rather than a referral-only fix, so a dropped password reset or firm invitation gets the same handling as a dropped referral (D-5). It returns a SendResult (ok/reason/permanent/attempts) rather than a bare bool; existing if not ok: call sites keep working because SendResult.__bool__ mirrors ok.

Classification (_classify_failure): a SparkPost 4xx response (other than 429) is permanent; 5xx, 429, requests timeout/connection errors, and anything unclassifiable are transient. A transmission the API accepts with zero accepted recipients is also treated as permanent — the address was rejected without raising.

In-process retry: a transient failure is retried within the same send_email call, up to MAX_SEND_ATTEMPTS (3) attempts total, sleeping RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS ([10, 20], ~30s total) between them. Only the final attempt's outcome is written to email_events — a send that recovers leaves no failed row and raises no alert. Because a single call can block for up to ~30s, no caller may await send_email (or a wrapper of it) synchronously from a request handler: every send — referrals (app/api/public/callbacks.py, app/api/public/appointments.py), conflict-check (app/api/admin/appointments.py), enrollment/user invitation and password reset (app/api/admin/organisations.py, app/api/firm/auth.py) and session-save (app/api/public/sessions.py) — runs via BackgroundTasks, off the request path. The four standalone senders that used to take the request's own DB session (send_enrollment_invitation, send_user_invitation, send_password_reset_email, send_session_save_email) now open and commit a short-lived session of their own instead, matching send_conflict_check_failed.

Permanent-failure alerting (_alert_permanent_failure, in email.py so it covers every send): fires immediately, once, via a bare send_email call — never through _send_and_log — so the alert itself cannot be classified and recursively re-alerted. The alert email identifies the recipient, template, transaction id (where there is one), firm/consumer context, failure reason and attempts.

Durable sweep (app/services/email_cycle.py, called from run_email_cycle): _retry_outcome_and_review_due re-invokes send_outcome_email/send_review_email for a transient failure whose template (Consumer-03/04/05/06/09/10/11) has no daily due-scan of its own, and _retry_referral_due does the same for the referral/confirmation templates (Firm-01/03, Consumer-01/07 — referral_emails.py), re-rendering from the stored Appointment + ChatSession via the same _callback_context/_firm_referral/_submission_data helpers dispatch_callback_emails / dispatch_select_emails use (Consumer-01 reconstructs every sibling firm in the submission, not just the one appointment the failed row happens to be keyed to; Firm-03 preserves the original send date in its "call by"/"pack by" copy, not the retry's own clock). Every other retriable template is already re-attempted naturally each time its own "due" gate re-runs should_attempt. should_attempt (workflow_emails.py) allows at most one attempt per London calendar day, only while the pair's first attempt is within RETRY_WINDOW (2 days) of now, and never for a permanent failure.

_retry_exhaustion_due then scans the log directly (not a "due" condition, so it also catches a send whose business trigger went moot before the window expired) for every failed transient send past RETRY_WINDOW — not only the templates the sweep above can reconstruct: whether a send is retriable never gates whether it is alerted. Appointment-scoped sends are deduped per (appointment_id, template) pair; the appointment-less standalone sends in email.py (password reset, contact form, session save, enrollment/user invitation, conflict-check) have nothing that ever retries them, so each failed row is its own complete attempt history, deduped by the row's own id. Either way CML gets one exception email via _send_retry_exhausted_alert, deduped by a marker row — keyed exp_<template> (appointment-scoped) or exp_<event id> (appointment-less), truncated to the template column's String(32). A prefix (exp_) rather than the original suffix scheme (template + "_exp", e.g. firm_02_exp): a suffix sits inside the consumer_*/firm_* prefixes /admin/email-log's template filter matches on and appeared as a pseudo-send. The marker is written unconditionally regardless of the alert's own outcome, so a failed alert send cannot trigger a re-alert next cycle — but it records that outcome truthfully (sent or failed, with the alert's own failure reason), and dedup is "does any row exist for this marker" rather than "does a sent row exist", so a truthful failed marker does not reopen the door to re-alerting. Both exhaustion scans exclude marker rows themselves (exp_%), so a failed marker is never picked up as a fresh candidate by a later pass.

already_attempted (workflow_emails.py) now counts only sent rows (issue #155 D-3) — previously a failed row also counted as "attempted", which was silently blocking retry of every workflow email that had ever failed once. Its remaining caller (workflow_emails.py:1118, suppressing a second Consumer-05 on the same submission) and the exhaustion-marker dedup above are the only sites where "did this genuinely succeed" is the right question; every retry/gating site uses should_attempt.

items.title: Email-event log & admin visibility
items.text: Every send writes one email_events row (recipient, template key, transaction id, API-level sent/failed — no delivery webhooks). A failed row also carries failure_reason (provider message, truncated to FAILURE_REASON_MAX_LENGTH/500 chars so a long message can't fail the write) and failure_classification (transient/permanent) — added by Alembic 0002, additive and nullable, so pre-0002 failed rows keep both columns NULL. GET /api/admin/email-log (X-Admin-Key) serves it paginated with filters (transaction, firm, template prefix, date range) and now includes the failure reason; the admin UI at /admin/email-log displays it and visually distinguishes failed rows from sent ones (no resend control — manual intervention only, D-10).

items.title: 12. Deployment & environment variables
items.text:
Two Railway services (backend, frontend) from Dockerfiles + a managed Postgres add-on. Backend start.sh runs alembic upgrade head then Uvicorn. Frontend NEXT_PUBLIC_* vars are build-time (set as Railway build variables, not runtime env).

Backend env (required unless noted):

Variable Req Purpose DATABASE_URL ✅ PG reference; postgresql:// auto-converted to postgresql+asyncpg:// by config.py SECRET_KEY ✅ JWT signing + HMAC follow-up tokens ADMIN_API_KEY ✅ X-Admin-Key value for /api/admin/* (empty ⇒ all admin routes 401) ENVIRONMENT ✅ production enables HSTS APP_URL ✅ Frontend URL (email links, deep links) API_URL ✅ Backend URL (logged on startup) CORS_ORIGINS ✅ Comma-separated; include Railway subdomain + custom domain during cutover SPARKPOST_API_KEY for email Empty ⇒ mock mode (logs only) SPARKPOST_FROM_EMAIL / _FROM_NAME for email Verified sender; defaults to noreply@mail.choosemylawyer.ai / Choose My Lawyer CML_AUDIT_EMAIL optional Audit BCC mailbox CML_EXCEPTION_EMAIL optional Firm-reporting exception mailbox (default info@choosemylawyer.ai, §11) CONTACT_EMAIL optional Destination for contact-form submissions (default info@choosemylawyer.ai) LOGIN_REQUEST_PARTICIPATING_EMAIL / LOGIN_REQUEST_LEAD_EMAIL optional "Request login details" relay (#192): a request matching an enrolled firm goes to the first, an unmatched one to the second; each defaults to CONTACT_EMAIL when unset ADDRESS_LOOKUP_API_KEY optional Ideal Postcodes key for the address-lookup proxy (§3, #127); empty ⇒ lookup unavailable, journey forms fall back to manual entry JWT_ALGORITHM / JWT_EXPIRY_HOURS optional HS256 / 8 (local docker-compose.yml overrides to 24 for dev convenience)

Frontend build variables (all NEXT_PUBLIC_* — baked into the bundle at build time via Dockerfile ARGs; changing one requires a rebuild, not a restart):

Variable Deployed value (production) Purpose NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL backend Railway URL Backend base URL for the API client NEXT_PUBLIC_GTM_ID GTM-KCRH887D Google Tag Manager container (consent-gated, §9); absent ⇒ GTM disabled NEXT_PUBLIC_META_PIXEL_ID not yet set Meta Pixel (consent-gated, §9); absent ⇒ Pixel disabled even with consent NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL not yet set Production-mode gate for robots.ts/metadata — must be https://choosemylawyer.ai at go-live or prod serves Disallow: / + noindex (issue #68); also needs an ARG adding to frontend/Dockerfile

Cloudflare DNS: choosemylawyer.ai proxied through Cloudflare in Full (strict) mode; CNAME the apex + www to the Railway frontend and api to the backend. Email TXT/CNAME records per §10.

items.title: Operational gotchas (lessons learned)
items.text:
1. NEXT_PUBLIC_* are build-time — set as Railway build variables; runtime-only env yields undefined in the browser bundle.
  2. Railway injects PORT — use ${PORT:-8000} in the backend CMD.
  3. DB URL protocol — Railway gives postgresql://; asyncpg needs postgresql+asyncpg:// (handled by config.py).
  4. Pre-launch schema policy — 0001_initial_schema.py is edited in place; an in-place edit no-ops on an already-migrated DB, so schema changes require a wipe-and-reseed (often surfacing as a 500 that looks like CORS). See docs/admin-guide.md.
  5. .env changes need docker-compose up -d (recreate), not restart.
  6. CORS must include both the Railway subdomain and the custom domain during cutover.

items.title: Known divergences (as-built vs older docs / spec)
items.text: • The CPS "Don't know" pricing consequence beyond "never apply the modifier" is still undefined — blocked on a CPS update (§6).
